messages:
Anya (docs): Heads-up: TS SDK 1.9.0 -> 2.0.0 will change streaming API semantics. Instead of raw string chunks, stream events now emit {delta, index, finished} objects. We published a short migration note: https://redwood.example.com/docs/sdk/ts/streaming-change

Diego (eng): Why the change?

Anya (docs): Allows deterministic reassembly, per-chunk metadata, and future token-level timing.

Priya (product): Is this breaking for customers using simple append-to-text logic? Need comms plan.

Diego (eng): We added an opt-in header X-Redwood-Legacy-Stream: true. Runtime accepts both for 30 days. Client 2.x has a compatibility flag `legacyStream: true` that reverts to raw strings. Default in 2.x is new object stream.

Lina (qa): Examples in examples/ts-streaming rely on string chunks. I'll open PRs to update them. Also adding an e2e that validates both stream shapes.

Anya (docs): Quick migration snippet added to quickstart:

```ts
// OLD streaming handler
client.streamGenerate(prompt, (chunk) => { buffer += chunk })

// NEW streaming handler
client.streamGenerate(prompt, (event) => { buffer += event.delta })
```

Anya (docs): Plan: console banner tomorrow, blog post + codemod, targeted email to TS-heavy tenants (>250k tokens/month). Runtime will start rejecting legacy header after 30 days unless tenant requests extension.

Priya (product): Good. Add a short FAQ about reconnect semantics and partial results.

Diego (eng): If customers hit issues, tag @Diego (eng) and @Priya (product) for rollback/grace. CLI-bot: changelog entry created -> https://redwood.example.com/changelog/ts-2.0-streaming

cli-bot: :white_check_mark: changelog updated by Anya (docs).
